evidence.approach: A new pure module, harness/calibration.py, reads every journal under docs/harness/history and derives the window, the escapes and the per-slice route evidence from records that already exist: the triage record's would_exclude, excluded_share, model_depth and criteria_answers, the review advance's findings, the route record's execution and the ticket's returns. Two record-shape gaps are closed first, because without them the evidence is silently favourable to the thing being calibrated: the review gate requires file on a finding at high or blocking severity, which seen-reviewer already emits, and harness return takes a repeatable --unmet naming the criteria a review found unmet, which is the only way escape kind two can be told from an ordinary return. The window is the most recent ten counted tickets rather than a stored counter, which is what makes criterion four fall out of the rule instead of needing state: go-live is go_live only when ten tickets are counted and none of them carries an escape, so an escape entering the window turns the verdict back to stay-shadow by itself and drops out again only after ten further tickets, which is the ticket's another ten. triage.run therefore asks calibration for the effective shadow: [review] triage_shadow or a stay-shadow verdict, so the founder's line stays the only way to go live and the return to shadow needs nobody. Nothing writes to thresholds.toml; the harness never rewrites its own rules. harness report --calibration renders the per-ticket and per-slice evidence with the rule printed beside it, as render_context already does for SEEN-099's budget, and the weekly report gains one line saying which shadow the triage is in and what put it there.
changes: harness/thresholds.toml: a new [calibration] section carrying window = 10, counted_from, the excluded tickets and why, the escape definition, and the triage and route go-live rules in words, written before any triage record it counts exists.
harness/thresholds.py: [calibration] and its keys in EXPECTED, so a half-written rule is fatal rather than defaulted, which is what the rest of this file already promises.

harness/calibration.py: new. counted() picks the window, escapes() finds both kinds and the unattributable remainder, slice_evidence() charges returns, findings and escaped defects to each slice of a route, verdict_triage() and verdict_routes() state go-live or stay-shadow by the rule, and effective_shadow() answers the one question triage asks.
harness/gates.py: a finding at high or blocking severity must carry file. Low and medium are left alone, because neither can ever be an escape.
harness/cli.py: return takes a repeatable --unmet, recorded in the return record as unmet_criteria; report takes --calibration and writes calibration.md and calibration.json.
harness/report.py: render_calibration for the new report, and one line in the weekly report naming the shadow the triage is in and the escape that put it there.
harness/triage.py: shadow comes from calibration.effective_shadow rather than straight from the threshold, and the triage record carries the reason it is in the shadow it is in.
harness/tests/test_calibration.py: new, covering the window, both escape kinds, the unattributable remainder, both verdicts, the automatic return to shadow and the report.
docs/harness/workflow.md and docs/harness/skill.md: the calibration window, what an escape is and who flips the switch; the skill copies are regenerated by sync.
harness/agents/seen-reviewer.md: file is required on a finding at high or blocking severity, regenerated into both assistants' copies by sync.
docs/harness/reports/calibration.md and .json: generated on this repository's own journals and committed, as the weekly and sprint reports already are.
tests_first: The window and both escape kinds. python3 -m pytest harness/tests/test_calibration.py -x. The RED must fail on harness/calibration.py not existing, then on a fixture where the reviewer filed a blocking finding in a file the triage's would_exclude names and the escape is not found.

A high or blocking finding with no file. python3 -m pytest harness/tests/test_calibration.py -k unattributable harness/tests/test_stage_gates.py -k finding. The RED must show the review gate accepting a blocking finding that names no file, which is the silent pass this ticket cannot measure through.

The two verdicts by the rule. python3 -m pytest harness/tests/test_calibration.py -k verdict. The RED must show nine counted tickets stating stay-shadow with the shortfall named, ten clean stating go-live, and ten with one escape stating stay-shadow naming it.

The automatic return to shadow. python3 -m pytest harness/tests/test_calibration.py -k shadow. The RED must show a triage record carrying shadow false while an escape sits in the window with [review] triage_shadow set false.
The report. python3 -m pytest harness/tests/test_calibration.py -k report. The RED must show harness report --calibration refused as an unknown flag.

slices.name: The rule and the evidence it will be read from
slices.red: test_calibration asserts an escape is found on a fixture where a blocking finding lands in a file the triage would have excluded. It must fail on harness/calibration.py not existing, and a second RED must show the review gate accepting a blocking finding that names no file.

slices.name: The report and the automatic return to shadow
slices.red: test_calibration asserts harness report --calibration writes the report and states the verdict, and that a triage runs in shadow while an escape sits in the window with the threshold set false. Both must fail: the flag is unknown and triage reads the threshold directly.

alternatives: Writing triage_shadow back to thresholds.toml when an escape is found, which is what automatically most plainly reads as. Rejected: the harness would be rewriting the rules it runs on, the file would stop being a diff a person reviews, and a report and a triage running at once would race over it. Computing the effective shadow leaves the founder's line the only writable one.

Storing the go-live as a marker record and counting escapes after it. Rejected: it needs a record kind nobody would otherwise write, and the window of the most recent ten already gives the ticket's another ten without any state.

Attributing a finding to a slice by searching its claim text for a path. Rejected: a guess dressed as a measurement. The reviewer already emits file, so the gate asks for it where it matters and the report names what it cannot place instead of counting it either way.

Counting SEEN-107, SEEN-108 and this ticket in the window. Rejected for the reason SEEN-098 wrote for itself: a ticket that built a tool was not worked with it, and all three wrote triage or route records while building the very things under calibration.
risks: Attribution is coarser than it reads. A return sends the whole ticket back and no record says which slice caused it, so a return is charged to every slice of the plan it returned and an escaped defect to every slice of its ticket, with findings the only per-slice measure. Mitigated by writing that into [calibration] route_rule and printing it under the table, so nobody reads a per-slice rate as a per-slice cause.

Ten tickets is a small window and one escape flips the triage back. That is the intended asymmetry, and the mitigation is that it costs a full review rather than a missed defect. Recorded here so the founder is not surprised by the first flip.

The route comparison can be empty: if no slice in the window is routed below the strongest tier there is nothing to compare, and a rate of zero against zero would read as a pass. Mitigated by stating not measurable with the count, the same way the context budget does below its minimum.

Requiring file on high and blocking findings could refuse a review a person wrote by hand. Mitigated by leaving low and medium alone and by the error naming the field and the reason, and seen-reviewer already emits it.
evidence.rollback: Nothing runs in production. The report is additive; the effective shadow is a widening of an existing true, so reverting the commit leaves every triage exactly where it is today. The only refusal added is file on a high or blocking finding, and reverting harness/gates.py restores the old behaviour with no journal to migrate, because records are append-only and nothing rereads them under the new rule.
tenant_tables: none: the harness writes journals and reports in the repository and touches no product table
